beats.head: Ardent Health Beats Again as Continental Fleet Upgrades Complete Final Phase
beats.body: Orla Halloran delivered another modest beat as the last tranche of Continental fleet upgrades rolled out on schedule, locking in higher recurring service revenue. Operating margin ticked up 90 basis points on the completed deployment. Halloran said the mature contract now provides 'a very quiet, very reliable base.'

beats.head: Blackhold Clears Defect Backlog as Redesigned Storage Cells Pass Safety Certification
beats.body: Perrin Vale confirmed the root-cause fix for the cell defect has cleared independent certification, ending the warranty-claim surge that battered recent results. The newly separated Storage unit will ship the redesigned cells starting next quarter, with Vale calling it 'the line under the crisis.' Management said reserved warranty funds came in $40M below the worst-case estimate.

beats.head: Brunmark Motors Beats as $1.9B Fleet Order Begins Feeding Revenue
beats.body: Iris Calvagh posted a second straight beat as initial deliveries against the landmark fleet contract lifted quarterly revenue 14%. The Veyra line ran at full capacity for the first time since its relaunch, and Calvagh raised full-year margin guidance. Parts and Power divisions also contributed with steady volume.

beats.head: Caldercraft Holdings Extends Weatherproof Range Into Household Line
beats.body: Vale Fenn introduced a weatherproof household goods sub-range, carrying the hardware line's proven coatings into storage bins, outdoor fixtures, and tool chests. The extension leverages existing supply relationships to keep costs contained ahead of the spring selling season. Fenn described it as 'a natural stretch, not a gamble.'

beats.head: Kessel Drive Faces Regulatory Probe as Vanta Ultra Packs Reported Overheating in Field
beats.body: Aldric Venn confirmed that safety regulators have opened a formal investigation into thermal incidents involving Vanta Ultra packs deployed under the $1.1B fleet pact. At least nine overheating events have been logged, prompting a precautionary charging-rate limit across affected fleets while the gigafactory ramp continues. Venn insisted the issue is 'a firmware calibration matter, not a cell flaw,' but the fleet customer has paused further intake pending findings.

beats.head: Kesselgrove Co. Launches Meridian Press Line as Third Bay Comes Online
beats.body: Orla Steg unveiled the Meridian series of industrial presses, the first new platform in nine years, timed to fill the freshly commissioned third bay. The line targets high-tonnage forming work and carries a 20% energy-efficiency gain over prior models. Steg said early order interest already covers the first two production runs.

beats.head: Korrwright Works Doubles Dovreux Frères Case Output to Ease Halbrook Waitlist
beats.body: Dunmore Carrow ordered a second production shift at the recently acquired Dovreux Frères workshop to address a swelling backlog for the prize-winning Halbrook Perpetual. The move adds roughly 4,000 cases of annual capacity and brings 60 additional artisans onto the payroll. Carrow said demand had 'outrun even our appetite.'

beats.head: Venline & Sons Extends Streak as Second Marden Cleanroom Reaches Full Output
beats.body: Mara Garr reported another slim beat as the second Marden cleanroom ramped to full production, adding consumable volume without disrupting the company's long unbroken run. Revenue rose 4% on the quarter. Garr reaffirmed the deliberate, incremental cadence that has defined the house for decades.

beats.head: Blackton Industries Opens Second Drivetrain Plant, Unveils Next-Gen Axle Module
beats.body: Sable Renwick marked the completion of the second drivetrain plant by launching a new integrated axle module aimed at expanding beyond the national fleet pact. The plant adds capacity for 400,000 units annually and Renwick said early interest from two regional fleet builders could broaden the customer base. The launch caps a fast-moving first year, though Renwick acknowledged the ramp has pushed capital spending to the top of guidance.

beats.head: Boreas Power Splits Compute and Power Units to Manage Coast-to-Coast Grid
beats.body: Mira Thorne unveiled a reorganization separating the compute-paired campus business from the core power and storage operation, creating dedicated leadership for each after the $6.8 billion third anchor pact. The move follows rapid expansion that left the single structure straining to service anchor tenants across four time zones. Thorne framed the split as a platform for the next wave of pacts rather than a pause.

beats.head: Halhold Systems Posts Record Quarter as Third Meridian Framework Ramps
beats.body: Ines Corvalan reported revenue of $1.9 billion, up 34% year-on-year, as the two Meridian framework wins moved into volume delivery ahead of schedule. Compute margins widened to 21%, the strongest since her arrival, and Corvalan raised full-year guidance while cautioning that expansion capital would keep free cash flow tight. The shift marks a full reversal from the turbulence that greeted her 2026 appointment.

beats.head: Halhold Works Recalls Reborn Aveline Line as Probe Confirms Fault, Fenwick Halts Sales
beats.body: Naomi Fenwick ordered a full recall of the relaunched Aveline devices after regulators confirmed a battery-connector defect tied to overheating in 47 reported units. The action pulls roughly 1.2 million devices from shelves barely months after the line's relaunch, wiping out the 'clean break' Fenwick had promised following Anselm Rocha's ouster. The company set aside $310 million for the recall and warned of a material hit to the medical-equipment division's supply timelines.

beats.head: Maison & Vale Lands $2.6B Household-Goods Giant Corriveau in Kessler's Biggest Swing Yet
beats.body: Rhys Kessler capped a year of relentless dealmaking with a $2.6 billion agreement to absorb household-goods maker Corriveau, nearly doubling Maison & Vale's shelf presence overnight. The purchase folds Corriveau's 14 factory sites into the recently opened Larenthal hub network, though analysts warn integration strain is mounting after three back-to-back acquisitions. Kessler told the board the deal 'completes the pantry,' but declined to rule out further targets.

beats.head: Stegforge Commissions Third Rail Plate Line Ahead of Schedule as Steg Adds Textile Capacity
beats.body: Aurelia Steg brought the third rail plate line online two months early, lifting total plate output by an estimated 40% to meet the consortium's multi-year offtake. Alongside the ramp, Steg quietly approved a modest expansion of the raw textiles mill, extending the disciplined build-out she has run for over a century. Management said the additions are fully covered by contracted demand, keeping the balance sheet conservative.

beats.head: Woldmark Misses Badly as Second Fab Delays Bite, Sonn's Big Bet Wobbles
beats.body: Petra Sonn's aggressive expansion backfired this quarter as construction setbacks at the second Meridian fab pushed deliveries under the $2.1 billion pact past deadline, triggering penalty clauses. Revenue fell 18% short of estimates at $640 million and Woldmark took a $150 million charge tied to the delay, sending the stock into its sharpest drop since Sonn's comeback declaration. Sonn insisted the fab will reach output within two quarters, but conceded the timeline 'left no room for error.'

beats.head: Aperture Compute Ordered to Halt Emberline Output as Regulators Widen Records Probe
beats.body: The Compute Safety Board issued a suspension order shutting Emberline's newest node line pending a full audit, after seized documents revealed altered inspection logs spanning eighteen months. Analysts estimate the halt strips $1.9B in annualized output, and two customers have invoked exit clauses. CEO Marisol Venn faces a board review as scrutiny turns from the facility to the executive suite.

beats.head: Vossenspire Supply Debuts Meridian-Bodied Flagship, First Fruit of Vehicles Division
beats.body: Vossenspire unveiled the Meridian Aurelian, a limited-run coachbuilt flagship pairing Corriveaux chassis work with Meridian Carrosserie bodywork, priced from $480,000 with just 250 units planned for the first year. CEO Quinn Marrow called it 'proof the Vehicles Division is more than the sum of its acquisitions,' with the launch order book reportedly covering nearly half of first-year output within weeks.

beats.head: Lhaus Industries Acquires Kellstrom Cell Maker Ardent Power in $9.2B Deal to Own Its Supply Chain
beats.body: Cole Brandt sealed the largest acquisition in company history, buying cell specialist Ardent Power for $9.2 billion to bring Kellstrom cell production fully in-house across its Power & Storage division. The deal locks in supply for the $4.3B fleet contract and gives Lhaus manufacturing capacity that management projects will lift Power margins by up to 400 basis points. Brandt framed the purchase as the anchor of a multi-year vertical-integration push.

beats.head: Gromford Works Ousts Halvard Pryce as Board Seeks Reset From Emblem Crisis
beats.body: The Gromford Works board removed chief executive Halvard Pryce after an emergency session, citing the deepening Emblem Signature sourcing scandal and mounting legal exposure now estimated near $900M. Incoming chief Adelheid Corven, a veteran of the group's Timepieces division, pledged an independent audit of every supply line and a suspension of the Signature Editions program pending review.
